Model — Encoder channel utilization

Per-block effective dimensionality of the encoder's own activations (head-independent), computed by SVD of each block's centered per-sample activations over every sample in keywords/terms/eval. Effective rank is the participation ratio (Σλ)²/Σλ² over that block's activation-covariance eigenvalues λ — an occupancy count robust to long tails, vs. Rank@95%, the raw number of components needed to explain 95% of variance. A block whose ratio sits well below 100% is spending channels that carry mostly redundant signal (over-provisioned); a block near 100% has no spare capacity left for encoding more (under-provisioned). See tools/block_capacity.py.

Model — Generator sensitivity (text vs. noise)

Takes 40 texts sampled from the gold set and runs every one through all 5 fixed noise seeds (CONST_Z — the same seeds the shipped web app renders as its card variants), then compares two things: how far the output moves when only the noise seed changes (same text), against how far it moves when only the text changes (same seed). Distances are mean pairwise Oklab distance over the full 9-dim card vector, matching model/color.py:energy_distance's unit.

MetricValue
Mean distance — same text, different noise seed0.099
Mean distance — different text, same noise seed0.198
Ratio (noise-driven / text-driven)0.50×
Output variance explained by text identity58.1%
Output variance explained by noise seed6.3%
text changes move the output at least as much as the noise seed does — conditioning looks intact.

Model — Generator energy distance by keyword

For each keyword under goals.yml's color generator.energy distance, up to 300 rows of data/data.jsonl whose text contains that keyword are sampled (deterministic, seeded), one ground-truth colour kept per row, and one generated palette drawn per row with fresh random generator noise. Energy distance is model/color.py:energy_distance between the two sets, in the same Oklab 9-dim card vector unit used elsewhere in this report.

Cross-lingual consistency (en vs he)

For each of 38 curated en/he word pairs (tools/report.py:LANG_PAIRS, each word verified present in data/keywords.jsonl / data/terms.jsonl for both languages), the English and Hebrew text are encoded separately and compared: cosine similarity of the raw TextEncoder embedding, Jaccard overlap of the top-5 EmojiHead predictions, StyleHead top-1 agreement, and ColorGen output distance (Oklab, zero noise vector so only text conditioning is compared, same 9-dim card unit as elsewhere in this report). Rows sorted by color distance, worst first. ⚠ flags a pair whose emoji predictions agree (Jaccard ≥ 0.2) but whose color distance is still above the mean — an emoji/color split like the one that motivated this section.

Mean encoder cosine 0.583, mean emoji Jaccard@5 0.270, style top-1 agreement 52.6%, mean color distance 0.284 (agreeing-emoji pairs, n=27: 0.286; disagreeing-emoji pairs: 0.278).
